age.evidence: C57BL/6J mice were between 5- and 6-week-old at arrival, after which they were acclimatized for one week

sex.evidence: Adult male C57BL/6J mice (Charles River, Kent, UK) were used for all experiments

dosing.doses_raw: 0.5, 1, and 2 mg/kg; main experiments used 2 mg/kg
dosing.evidence: (±)-DOI hydrochloride was dissolved in 0.9% saline... Each animal received only one injection, administered intraperitoneally at 5 ml/kg. A 2 mg/kg dose of (±)-DOI was used for all experiments as it resulted in near-peak acute psychedelic effects

handling.evidence: using a standardized way of tunnel handling to minimize stress

group_housing.evidence: All animals were housed in groups of 3-4 in open-top cages

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12h light/dark cycle (lights off at 7PM), with all procedures done during the light phase

enrichment_housing.evidence: open-top cages with sawdust and enrichment available (sizzle nest, and cardboard tunnel and house)

assays.assay_description: Mice placed in a 42 × 20 × 20 cm clear Plexiglass box and video-recorded for the first 30 min after a single i.p. injection; head-twitches and ear-scratches manually scored. Includes a dose-response cohort (0.5, 1, 2 mg/kg) and confirmation in the three main two-step cohorts.

setup_habituation.evidence: habituated to the recording box... 5 min of free exploration before injection

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were video-recorded while freely moving in the box

food_restriction.evidence: no food in the recording box

water_restriction.evidence: no water in the recording box

time_to_assay.evidence: recorded in the first 30 min after injection

sample_size.evidence: n group = 8 per dose for dose-response; n Veh = 13, n DOI = 13 (Exp1); n Veh = 15, n DOI = 14 (Exp2); n Veh = 13, n DOI = 14 (Exp3)

outcomes.summary: DOI dose-dependently increased head-twitches and ear-scratches relative to saline; 2 mg/kg produced near-peak responses and was used as the standard dose.
outcomes.evidence: (±)-DOI induced a high frequency head-twitch response... and ear-scratch response

B1_num_measures.evidence: head-twitches and ear-scratches were video recorded and quantified

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Reported as total counts over 30 min

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded as ethological per rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: quantified manually by the same trained experimenter

E3_bedding.evidence: no bedding reported in the recording box

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material in test box

D3_recording_days.evidence: Each animal received only one injection

assays.assay_description: Operant task in custom 12×12 cm boxes with 5 nose-poke ports; water-restricted mice initiate trial, choose left/right (step 1) leading probabilistically to up/down step-2 ports for water reward. Reward probabilities reversed serially; a single novel transition reversal (TR) was introduced at 1 day (Exp 2) or 1 week (Exp 1 & 3) post-DOI. 90-min sessions, daily.

setup_habituation.evidence: Training consisted of multiple stages with increasing complexity

food_restriction.evidence: All animals had a food pellet available in the operant box during behavioural training and testing

water_restriction.evidence: Mice tested in the two-step task were water-restricted for motivation

time_to_assay.evidence: starting one day later, continued tracked their daily task performance over the course of one week; transition reversal one day (Exp 2) or one week (Exp 1 & 3) post-treatment

sample_size.evidence: Exp 1: nVeh=13, nDOI=13; Exp 2: nVeh=15, nDOI=14; Exp 3: nVeh=13, nDOI=14

outcomes.summary: DOI did not change overall accuracy or trial counts, but when a novel transition reversal was introduced 1 week post-dose (Exp 1), DOI-treated mice adapted faster and uniquely began learning from reward omissions. No effect when reversal occurred 1 day post-dose (Exp 2). When mice received no intervening task experience (Exp 3), DOI mildly slowed adaptation, indicating a time- and experience-dependent effect.
outcomes.statistics: Exp 1 Transition×Outcome P=0.004; Omission-by-transition slope=-0.112 [-0.192,-0.032], P=0.007; Exp 2 all P>0.5; Exp 3 Vehicle line vs one-phase P=0.016; 3-way ANOVA Drug×Experiment P=0.035, ηp²=0.08
outcomes.evidence: (±)-DOI's effects on cognitive flexibility were contingent on the timing between drug treatment and the novel reversal, as well as on the nature of the intervening experience

B1_num_measures.evidence: trials, correct choices, reward reversals, choice probability trajectories, tau-fast/slow adaptation constants, and logistic regression predictors (Outcome, Transition, Transition×Outcome, Reward-by-transition, Omission-by-transition)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: choice probability in the first 20 post-reversal trials; time series of regression coefficients fitted with nonlinear regression

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: Trial-by-trial logistic regression on stay/switch sequences based on previous transitions and outcomes; lagged regression analysis

B7_automated_classification.evidence: pyControl for trial events; no pose estimation or ML classifier of behavioural states

B8_multivariate.evidence: Logistic regression on trial features and exponential fits; no PCA/UMAP/clustering of behavioural profiles

E6_spatial.evidence: Single operant chamber with ports on one wall, no physical dividers

E7_social_context.evidence: Focal mouse alone in operant box

E8_food_water.evidence: All animals had a food pellet available in the operant box during behavioural training and testing; water rewards delivered in-task

D1_continuity.evidence: daily sessions across pre-drug, post-drug week, and 2 post-TR weeks

D2_session_duration.evidence: 90 min sessions were used at the final training stage and throughout subsequent testing

D3_recording_days.evidence: ~27 training sessions plus one post-drug week and two post-TR weeks of daily testing

D4_baseline.evidence: Pre-drug performances were compared via unpaired t-tests / RM ANOVA

D5_followup.evidence: Testing continued from 24 h to 3 weeks post-injection

judge_notes: Excluded ex vivo MRI analyses (anatomical/structural endpoint, not a behavioural assay) per rubric.

Consolidated two assays: head-twitch/ear-scratch response and the two-step probabilistic reversal learning task. All three two-step experiments (different TR timing/experience) were merged into a single assay entry per rubric (same paradigm, different manipulations).

Adopted gptoss's higher B1 score (7+) for the two-step task since the paper reports trials, correct choices, reward reversals, choice probability, tau-fast/slow, and 4-5 logistic-regression predictors — clearly ≥7 measures.
B3 set to Yes for two-step task: trial-by-trial lagged logistic regression on stay/switch sequences qualifies as transitional/sequential analysis.
E6 scored 0 for the operant box: ports on a single wall do not constitute physical compartments separated by walls.
water_restriction set to 'before' for the two-step task (chronic water-restriction protocol for motivation, water available as reward during session).
Age range extended to cover acclimation + ~3-4 weeks training; conservative bound.
